headline: PSX slides for a third sharp down-leg in six sessions as the US-Iran conflict refuses to cool, KSE-100 closing 173,636.07 (-0.97%) with autos, cement, banks, OMCs and refiners all in the red.
summary: KSE-100 closed at 173,636.07, down 1,692.75 points (-0.97%) — the third sharp down-day in six sessions, driven by the escalating US-Iran conflict, not domestic news. Brent crude is still up over 15% this month and global risk gauges ticked higher too. Pakistan's own backdrop adds little cushion: CPI at 11.1%, SBP holding at 11.5% into its September 14 meeting, and an IMF review still pending. Autos, cement, banks, OMCs and refiners all sold off today. The desk is leaning defensive — favoring cheap, dividend-covered names and proven technical setups, while flagging that 263 of 456 tracked stocks haven't had a fresh price since August 26, so today's read leans on confirmed news and live triggers, not stale charts.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Rates staying high into the Sept 14 SBP decision keeps bank margins fat, and names like HBL, UBL, MCB and BOP screen cheap with covered double-digit dividends — worth watching on today's weakness, selectively, not as a broad basket.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas Exploration (E&P)
sectors.why: Brent is still up over 15% this month, which should help OGDC/PPL/MARI margins, but today's war-driven selloff hit them anyway (OGDC -2.38%, PPL -1.88%) — the oil tailwind isn't showing up in the price action right now.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: NRL screens cheap and just fired a live breakout trigger, but PRL cratered -10% today on the same fear — this is a name-by-name story, not a sector-wide bid.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Thin margins meet fuel-cost exposure; the macro desk has flagged OMCs to avoid for weeks, and today's tape just confirmed it.

sectors.name: Automobile Assemblers
sectors.why: Rate-sensitive and import-cost exposed, and autos were named among today's hardest-hit sectors — GAL's technical setup below is the lone exception, not a sector call.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-cost exposed and rate-sensitive, cement was named among today's red sectors, and most names carry thin margins with little dividend cushion to lean on.

watchlist.angle: A fresh 55-day Donchian breakout fired today — a live desk trigger, medium confidence, backed by a 60-trade sample with a 57% out-of-sample hit rate — and the stock is cheap on paper (P/E 7.1, bottom third of PSX). Refineries are one of macro's selectively-favoured pockets right now.
watchlist.risk: The refinery sector just got hammered — PRL alone fell 10% today on the same US-Iran fear — so this breakout is fighting the tape, not riding it. Margins are thin (1% net) and there's no dividend to cushion a stall.

watchlist.angle: The strongest live signal on the desk today: a 55-day Donchian breakout with the best backtested payoff of today's four active triggers (3.62% net expectancy, 75% out-of-sample hit rate), in Technology & Communication — a sector not named among today's casualties.
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals are a real caution flag — the company is loss-making and pays no dividend, so this is a pure technical bet with only 13 historical trades behind the setup. A stall here has no fundamental floor underneath it.

watchlist.angle: A trend/momentum combo trigger is firing (medium confidence, 38-trade sample, 60% out-of-sample hit), and the fundamentals aren't bad either — cheap at P/E 5.5 with a healthy 12.5% net margin.
watchlist.risk: Automobile assemblers are named as one of today's hit sectors — this trigger is swimming against a sector-wide selloff, and results are pencilled in for around Sept 29 (an unconfirmed, scraped estimate) which could cut either way.

watchlist.angle: No live technical trigger here, but the fundamentals screen well — cheap at P/E 6.3, improving forward earnings, a covered dividend — and it carries one of the only confirmed, dated catalysts on the board this week: ex-dividend Sept 10, book closure Sept 11.
watchlist.risk: Beta of 1.2 means it swings more than the market — in a risk-off tape like today's that cuts both ways, and banks broadly took some damage today (NBP -1.27%) even where the fundamentals hold up fine.

catalysts.event: SBP Monetary Policy Committee decision — CPI at 11.1%, cut odds effectively off the table
IMF 4th EFF / 3rd RSF review mission expected (date unconfirmed) — roughly $1.2bn at stake
GAL results expected (scraped estimate, not yet confirmed)
TPLT results expected (scraped estimate, not yet confirmed)

risks: The US-Iran conflict is still escalating, not resolving — three sharp down-legs in six sessions is the market telling you it hasn't priced a resolution yet.

Data health is degraded: 263 of 456 tracked symbols haven't had a fresh price since August 26, so today's read leans on the confirmed KSE-100 close and live triggers rather than a full technical scan of the market.

SBP is holding at 11.5% with CPI at 11.1% and no near-term rate relief in sight — that keeps pressure on rate-sensitive sectors (autos, cement, small banks) regardless of what happens with the conflict.
